title: migration backlog preview: default-mode alias-collision refusal carries no structured input, so a caller cannot tell renumbering from a dual claim
description:
QCLI-256 gave the default-mode alias-collision refusal prose naming both causes (positional renumbering vs a genuine dual claim in the destination) and both remedies. That is a good human message and it stops there: the refusal carries no `input`, so two purpose-built repros return the same sentence differing only in the quoted id, and a programmatic caller cannot branch without parsing prose.

Asked by lore-cli 2026-09-17 as a QUESTION, not a defect report, while shipping `lore init --migrate-backlog`s wizard (LCLI-466, PR #137). Lore is unblocked and needs nothing: it classifies nothing from the default-mode message, asks the operator, then re-runs the preservation-mode preview (which mutates nothing) and lets that be the authority.

Their repros re-run independently here against the installed 0.7.1 binary (/Users/jdnewhouse/.nvm/versions/node/v24.20.0/bin/quest), not accepted from their transcripts, because they flagged the originals were produced by a subagent:

- Repro A, positional renumbering: source TASK-1, TASK-1.1, TASK-2, TASK-3 into an EMPTY TASK-prefixed workspace. exit 5, `Alias collision: "TASK-2" conflicts with "TASK-2"`, no `input`.
- Repro B, genuine dual claim: destination already holding live TASK-1/TASK-2. exit 5, `Alias collision: "TASK-1" conflicts with "TASK-1"`, no `input`.
- Preservation mode on A: exit 0 with a plan, `renumbered: [{sourceIdentifier: "TASK-1.1", reason: "dotted_subtask_translated"}]`.
- Preservation mode on B: exit 5 WITH `input.collisions` (both pairs) and `input.unpreservable: []`.

So the asymmetry is real and it runs the wrong way: the refusal that CAN be resolved by a flag is the unstructured one.

The answer to "does Quest genuinely not know at that point" is NO -- it can know, and this should not be written off as unknowable.

1. The discriminator exists and is discarded. `assertAliasesAvailable` (src/domain/records.ts:106-124) seeds `seen` from `existing` (the destinations occupied ids and aliases), then adds each candidate as it iterates. At the throw, `seen.get(entry.key)` resolved either from the seed (a destination claim) or from a previously-added candidate (an internal renumbering collision). The function knows which and throws a string keeping neither. Repro A proves the candidate-vs-candidate path is reachable with an empty destination, where `occupied` is necessarily empty; repro B proves the candidate-vs-occupied path.

2. Stronger, and this is the one to implement: Quest can compute the exact answer rather than infer it. At the default-mode throw site in `previewImport` (src/application/migration/backlog-public.ts), everything `previewWithPreservedIds` needs is already in hand -- `snapshot`, `occupied`, `existing.taskRecords`. It is read-only, and it collects every collision instead of failing fast. So the refusal can speculatively run the preservation analysis and report whether preservation would resolve this as a measured fact.

Prefer (2) over (1). (1) is necessary but NOT sufficient: a candidate-vs-candidate collision can still be unresolvable by preservation, because preservation can independently refuse on an unpreservable record (unresolvable parent) or on preserved ids that collide among themselves. Shipping `cause` off the seed/candidate distinction alone would sometimes promise `preservationWouldResolve: true` and then refuse on the retry -- the exact failure QCLI-256 was raised to stop, in a new costume.

Open design question, the one genuine complication: preservation requires `--source-family` and imports one family per run, so a multi-family source has no single answer. Options are to answer for the family of the colliding record, or to report per family. That is a design call, not an unknowability.

Consumer-authored acceptance example (lore-cli):

{"error_type":"conflict","message":"Alias collision: ...",
 "input":{"cause":"positional_renumbering","preservationWouldResolve":true,
          "collisions":[{"candidate":"TASK-2","conflictsWith":"TASK-2"}]}}

with "cause":"destination_claim" / preservationWouldResolve:false for the other shape. The prose message can stay exactly as it is for humans; this is additive.

Envelope note: this adds keys under an existing `input` object on the ERROR envelope, not a new top-level key, so the contractVersion index-1 and principal-last constraints in the repository profile are untouched. But opum-cli-e2es `check.errorEnvelope` allow-lists top-level error keys only, and `input` is already in that list -- confirm before shipping.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The default-mode alias-collision refusal from `migration backlog preview` carries a structured `input` that distinguishes a positional-renumbering collision from a genuine destination claim, without a caller parsing the prose message

Whatever the refusal reports about whether preservation would resolve the collision is computed from the preservation analysis itself, not inferred from the seed-vs-candidate distinction alone -- so a refusal claiming preservation would resolve it is not followed by a preservation run that refuses

Repro A (source TASK-1, TASK-1.1, TASK-2, TASK-3 into an empty TASK-prefixed workspace) and repro B (destination already holding live TASK-1/TASK-2) are both covered by tests, and the two produce DIFFERENT structured output rather than the same sentence with a different id

The multi-family case is decided and documented: either the refusal answers for the family of the colliding record, or it reports per family, and the chosen behavior is stated where a caller will read it

If any part is judged genuinely not knowable at that point, that is documented in the migration guidance so the next caller does not rediscover it, rather than left implied by a message that names two causes it cannot distinguish
The human-readable message from QCLI-256 is preserved unchanged; this is additive
bun run check exits 0 with the new tests included
